description: Fig. 15 is a single-panel grouped bar chart comparing the model prediction difference of two machine-learning models at three test temperatures. The y-axis is labelled "Value/MPa" with tick marks printed at 0, 20 and 40; the x-axis carries three categorical groups labelled 750 °C, 800 °C and 850 °C. The legend has two entries: "Extra Trees" (bars filled with a red-to-white vertical gradient) and "GA-Extra Trees" (bars filled with a blue-to-white vertical gradient). Every bar carries a printed numeric label: at 750 °C the Extra Trees difference is 34 and the GA-Extra Trees difference is 12; at 800 °C the values are 31 and 10; at 850 °C the values are 36 and 19. In all three temperature groups the GA-Extra Trees bar is markedly shorter than the Extra Trees bar — roughly one third of its height — and all bars lie between the 0 and 40 gridlines, well below the top of the frame. Subtracting each printed pair gives a reduction of 22 MPa at 750 °C, 21 MPa at 800 °C and 17 MPa at 850 °C, i.e. the figure demonstrates that genetic-algorithm hyperparameter optimisation of the Extra Trees model reduces the difference between predicted and real yield strength across the whole test-temperature range.

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled "Value/MPa" with printed tick marks only at 0, 20 and 40.
The x-axis shows three evaluation temperatures: 750 °C, 800 °C and 850 °C.
The legend contains exactly two entries: "Extra Trees" (red-gradient bars) and "GA-Extra Trees" (blue-gradient bars).
At 750 °C the printed bar labels are 34 (Extra Trees) and 12 (GA-Extra Trees).
At 800 °C the printed bar labels are 31 (Extra Trees) and 10 (GA-Extra Trees).
At 850 °C the printed bar labels are 36 (Extra Trees) and 19 (GA-Extra Trees).
The GA-Extra Trees bar is shorter than the Extra Trees bar in every one of the three temperature groups.
The largest printed Extra Trees difference is 36 (850 °C) and the smallest printed GA-Extra Trees difference is 10 (800 °C).
The printed bar pairs imply reductions of 22 MPa (750 °C), 21 MPa (800 °C) and 17 MPa (850 °C) when going from Extra Trees to GA-Extra Trees.
The caption describes the figure only as "Comparison of model prediction difference" and does not state units, values or which quantity the difference refers to.
The citing text states that the difference between the predicted value and the real value was reduced by 22 MPa at 750 °C, 21 MPa at 800 °C and 17 MPa at 850 °C, matching the printed bar pairs.
The citing text states that the contribution values of various strengthening mechanisms were used as input features and the YS as the output feature for the Extra trees and GA-Extra trees models.
The citing text asserts that the framework predicts YS of Medium-manganese low-density steel and can be well transferred to it.
